intro: The Chargers finally won, snapping an 11-game skid on Monday night in Baltimore, while New England waits on word about Drake Maye's ankle. Buffalo and San Francisco sit at the top of the board as the 49ers head to Mexico City. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Chargers end 11-game skid with 23-20 win over Ravens
top.dek: Los Angeles won for the first time in 331 days, since Dec. 21, 2025. Tarheeb Still forced a fumble on Baltimore's last drive and Elijah Molden recovered it. The Ravens have now lost five straight.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Patriots fear Drake Maye broke his ankle
top.dek: Maye left the 35-10 loss to Detroit in Munich in the first quarter after a sack by Aidan Hutchinson. Sources told ESPN the team fears a fracture that could end his season. Coach Mike Vrabel called it a lower leg injury after the game.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Trevor Lawrence throws for 352 yards in Jacksonville's 40-23 win
top.dek: Lawrence threw three touchdowns as the Jaguars moved to 7-2 in Nashville. Jacksonville has scored 30 or more in four straight games and leads the AFC South by four games.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 325: Josh Allen's touchdown record through 10 seasons
top.dek: Allen passed Peyton Manning for the most regular-season touchdowns by any player in his first 10 seasons. He added two rushing scores in Buffalo's 31-12 win over the Jets.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: 49ers and Vikings meet in Mexico City on Sunday night
top.dek: San Francisco plays Minnesota on Sunday, Nov. 22 at Estadio Azteca, a 5:20 p.m. PT kickoff, or 8:20 p.m. ET, on NBC. The 49ers practice in Colorado Springs first. Watch their offense against a Vikings defense that sacked Green Bay eight times.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Bills hit 8-1, best start since 1991

stories.text: Bills beat Jets 31-12 for the best start in 35 years
stories.summary: Buffalo won at MetLife on Sunday and moved to 8-1, its best opening since 1991. Josh Allen ran for two touchdowns and threw for another, and James Cook sealed it with a 74-yard run in the fourth quarter. Coach Joe Brady is now 5-0 on the road in his first season.

stories.text: Alford and Williams hurt in New Jersey
stories.summary: Cornerback Dee Alford left with a concussion and linebacker Dorian Williams has a calf injury. Neither has an official designation yet. Watch the Wednesday practice report before Miami comes to town.

stories.text: James Cook runs for 157 on 18 carries
stories.summary: Cook broke the Jets open with a 74-yard touchdown run, the longest of his career. He finished with 157 yards and a score on 18 carries. Buffalo needed the ground game while Allen threw for only 196 yards on 21 attempts.

stories.text: 325: Allen's touchdown record through 10 seasons
stories.summary: Allen now has 325 regular-season touchdowns, passing Peyton Manning for the most by any player in his first 10 seasons. He added two rushing scores against the Jets.

stories.text: Dolphins visit Highmark Stadium on Sunday
stories.summary: Buffalo hosts Miami on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1:00 p.m. on CBS. Early lines have the Bills favored by 16.5 points. Miami starts a backup quarterback.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Dolphins cut kicker after 24-22 loss

stories.text: Missed kicks sink Miami in Indianapolis
stories.summary: The Dolphins lost 24-22 to the Colts and fell to 1-8. Zane Gonzalez missed two field goals and an extra point, and Miami waived him afterward. Coach Jeff Hafley said a new kicker decision is pending.

stories.text: Sieler done for the year, two more linemen hurting
stories.summary: Defensive tackle Zach Sieler is out for the season. Zeek Biggers (knee) and Jordan Phillips (arm) are getting more tests, and Hafley said he has concerns about both. Quarterback Malik Willis is on injured reserve with a groin injury.

stories.text: Rookie Chris Johnson scores on a 59-yard pick-six
stories.summary: Johnson returned an interception 59 yards for a touchdown. It was the first pick-six by a Dolphins rookie since Minkah Fitzpatrick in 2018.

stories.text: 209: Kyle McCord's yards in his first start
stories.summary: McCord completed 17 of 32 passes with no interceptions and ran in a touchdown. His 209 yards rank second among Dolphins quarterbacks in a debut, behind Ryan Tannehill's 219. He also lost a fumble that Indianapolis returned for a score.

stories.text: Miami visits Buffalo on Sunday
stories.summary: The Dolphins play at the Bills on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1:00 p.m. on CBS. McCord is expected to start at least three more games. Miami also needs a kicker.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Maye feared out with broken ankle

stories.text: Patriots fear Drake Maye broke his ankle
stories.summary: Maye left the 35-10 loss to Detroit in Munich in the first quarter after a sack by Aidan Hutchinson. Sources told ESPN the team fears a fracture that could end his season. Coach Mike Vrabel said he did not think the hit was intentional.

stories.text: A.J. Brown hurts hamstring in his return
stories.summary: Brown came back from a two-game knee absence and caught two passes for 27 yards before a hamstring injury ended his day. Vrabel did not know the severity after the game. Maye's injury is the larger concern.

stories.text: Tommy DeVito steps in for Maye
stories.summary: DeVito went 12 of 24 for 81 yards with a touchdown and an interception after Maye left. Rookie Behren Morton is also on the roster, and the team may add another quarterback.

stories.text: 43: Maye's consecutive starts, third longest in the NFL
stories.summary: Maye carried a 43-game starting streak into Munich, the third longest in the league. It is now in doubt with the ankle injury.

stories.text: Bye week, then Sunday night at the Chargers
stories.summary: New England is off in Week 11. It plays at the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29 at 8:20 p.m. ET (5:20 p.m. PT) on NBC at SoFi Stadium.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Jets wait on Geno Smith's ankle

stories.text: Jets lose fifth straight, 31-12 to Bills
stories.summary: New York fell to 2-8 and has gone nine straight quarters without a touchdown. Coach Aaron Glenn is 5-22 overall and 0-9 in the AFC East. Jason Sanders kicked four field goals.

stories.text: Geno Smith will start if his ankle allows
stories.summary: Smith hurt his left ankle in the third quarter, after clearing a concussion check at halftime. Tests showed no major injury, and Glenn said he starts against the Chargers if healthy. Receiver Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) and guard Dylan Parham (knee) also got hurt.

stories.text: Rookie Cade Klubnik makes his NFL debut
stories.summary: The fourth-round pick went 11 of 20 for 137 yards with an interception and took three sacks. He moved New York into field-goal range on his first series but could not find the end zone.

stories.text: 64: plays in opponent territory without a touchdown
stories.summary: Over the last two games the Jets ran 64 plays in opposing territory and never scored a touchdown. They lost both games by at least 17 points despite four scoring drives in each.

stories.text: Jets travel to face the Chargers on Sunday
stories.summary: New York plays at Los Angeles on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 4:05 p.m. on FOX. Watch the quarterback decision between Smith and Klubnik.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Ravens drop fifth straight to winless Chargers

stories.text: Ravens lose fifth straight, 23-20 to Chargers
stories.summary: Baltimore fell to 4-6 on Monday night, its first five-game losing streak since 2021. Jacoby Brissett led the offense in his Ravens debut, but a late Zay Flowers fumble on a strip by Tarheeb Still gave the Chargers the ball and the win. The Chargers had entered the night 0-8.

stories.text: Brissett limps off early after hit to the knee
stories.summary: Brissett went down in the first quarter when guard Vega Ioane was pushed back into his leg, and he limped off. A doctor cited by Yahoo described a mild MCL stress. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins was ruled out with a knee injury before the game and has missed four straight. Lamar Jackson remains out with a thumb injury.

stories.text: Brissett throws for 340 yards in his debut
stories.summary: Brissett completed 33 of 49 passes for 340 yards with one interception, the second most yards of his career. Mark Andrews posted season highs of eight catches and 82 yards. Mike Green added two sacks and leads the team with 5.5.

stories.text: 16: rushing yards, third lowest in franchise history
stories.summary: The Ravens ran 15 times for 16 yards against the Chargers. Derrick Henry scored twice but gained 10 yards on 10 carries. His touchdowns moved him past Marshall Faulk into seventh on the NFL's career list.

stories.text: Ravens visit Panthers Sunday at 1 p.m. on FOX
stories.summary: Baltimore plays Carolina (4-5) on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET at Bank of America Stadium, on FOX. Watch Brissett's knee all week. The Ravens have not scored more than 13 points in four of their five losses.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Bengals bury Steelers, take AFC North lead

stories.text: Bengals rout Steelers 38-18, own the division
stories.summary: Cincinnati led 24-3 at the half and outgained Pittsburgh 337 yards to 40 in the first two quarters. The win is the Bengals' fifth in a row and puts them alone in first place in the AFC North at 7-2.

stories.text: Risner leaves with a knee injury
stories.summary: Starting guard Dalton Risner left Sunday night's game with a knee injury. Tee Higgins looked to be limping late but still caught five passes for 66 yards. Watch the practice report this week for both.

stories.text: Chase catches 11 for 231 against Pittsburgh
stories.summary: Ja'Marr Chase had his biggest game of the season with 11 receptions and 231 yards. Joe Burrow went 35 of 44 for 409 yards and four touchdowns, tying Peyton Manning's record of five straight games with at least four offensive touchdowns.

stories.text: 5: straight 30 point games, a Bengals first
stories.summary: Cincinnati has scored at least 30 points in five consecutive games, a franchise record. Burrow also became the third passer in league history with 20 touchdown passes over a five-game span, joining Tom Brady and Peyton Manning.

stories.text: Bengals visit Commanders on Monday night
stories.summary: Cincinnati travels to Northwest Stadium in Landover to face Washington on Monday, Nov. 23 at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. The Commanders are 3-5-1 and rank near the bottom of the league against the pass.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Browns erase 17-0 hole, beat Texans 27-24

stories.text: Browns rally from 17-0 to beat Texans
stories.summary: Cleveland came back from a 17-point deficit, its largest comeback since 2014. Quinshon Judkins ran in a 5-yard touchdown with 53 seconds left. The Browns are 4-0 at home and hold the final AFC wild-card spot.

stories.text: Watson back from concussion, no new injuries reported
stories.summary: Deshaun Watson missed Week 9 with a concussion and started against Houston. Neither the NFL.com recap nor the Bleacher Report roundup listed new Browns injuries from the game. The bye week gives the roster extra time to heal.

stories.text: Schwesinger leads all players with 13 tackles
stories.summary: Linebacker Carson Schwesinger made 13 stops, the most in the game. Denzel Ward allowed four catches for 16 yards on nine targets and broke up three passes. Cleveland pressured C.J. Stroud on 23 of 42 dropbacks.

stories.text: 6: wins, all sealed on fourth quarter drives
stories.summary: Every one of the Browns' six victories has come on a game winning drive in the fourth quarter. Watson threw for 312 yards and ran for 49 more with a touchdown, and Harold Fannin Jr. caught seven passes for 91 yards.

stories.text: Browns on bye, then host Raiders Nov. 29
stories.summary: Cleveland is off in Week 11. The Browns return Sunday, Nov. 29 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX at Huntington Bank Field against the Las Vegas Raiders, then host Cincinnati on Dec. 6.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers' offense stalls in 38-18 loss

stories.text: Steelers fall 38-18 to Bengals, lose division lead
stories.summary: Pittsburgh punted on its first three drives and had about 40 yards of offense at halftime. It did not record a first down until its third possession. The Bengals now hold first place and have beaten the Steelers twice this season.

stories.text: McCormick carted off with ankle injury
stories.summary: Left guard Mason McCormick left with a right ankle injury and an air cast, and Spencer Anderson replaced him. McCormick had played every offensive snap this season. Pat Freiermuth called it a really big loss, and the team has given no timeline.

stories.text: Rodgers starts 0 for 8 in worst opening of career
stories.summary: Aaron Rodgers missed his first eight throws, the worst start of his career, and was pressured on 46.9 percent of his dropbacks. He completed four passes for 25 yards in the first half. DK Metcalf had two catches for 54 yards on six targets.

stories.text: 15: rushing yards for Jaylen Warren on seven carries
stories.summary: Warren gained 15 yards on seven attempts and Rico Dowdle added 25 on five. Without a run game, Pittsburgh trailed Burrow by 277 passing yards at halftime, the third largest gap between opposing quarterbacks since 2000.

stories.text: Steelers visit Eagles Sunday at 1 p.m. on CBS
stories.summary: Pittsburgh plays at Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. The NFL moved the game up from 4:25 p.m. and off national TV. The Eagles are 2-7 coming off their bye.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Texans blow 17-point lead in Cleveland

stories.text: Texans give away a 17-0 lead and fall to Cleveland
stories.summary: Houston scored on its first three drives, then watched Cleveland outscore it 27-7 the rest of the way in a 27-24 loss. The Texans are 3-6 and 1-5 in one-score games. Next Gen Stats now puts their playoff odds at 18% with eight games left.

stories.text: Woody Marks leaves Cleveland game with a concussion
stories.summary: Running back Woody Marks exited with a concussion, and Emari Demercado took over as the lead back. Marks will need to clear the league protocol before he can play Thursday night against Indianapolis. The first official Week 11 injury report is still to come.

stories.text: Nico Collins goes quiet after a fast start
stories.summary: Collins caught 7 passes for 79 yards and a touchdown in the first half. After halftime he managed 2 catches for 15 yards as the offense stalled. Houston will need him involved early and late against Indianapolis.

stories.text: 13: penalties flagged on Houston for 112 yards
stories.summary: The Texans took 13 penalties for 112 yards against Cleveland, a total the Houston Press says may have cost them the game. They also lost five games in the first nine weeks while tied or leading inside the final two minutes, the only team to do that in 50 seasons.

stories.text: Thursday night host date with Indianapolis
stories.summary: Houston hosts the Colts on Thursday, Nov. 19 at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. The Texans get a short week to clean up the penalties and finish a lead.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts snap skid with a 24-22 win over Miami

stories.text: Colts end their losing streak, barely
stories.summary: Indianapolis beat Miami 24-22 to end a skid that began in Week 4. Seth McGowan ran for 77 yards and a score, and CJ Allen had nine tackles and a sack. The offense still struggled, and the Colts stand at 3-7.

stories.text: Gardner, Ward and Raimann all hurt in Miami win
stories.summary: Cornerbacks Sauce Gardner (calf) and Charvarius Ward (shin) left in the third quarter. Left tackle Bernhard Raimann went out with a concussion after six snaps, and Jalen Travis was already sidelined. Their availability for Thursday in Houston is unclear.

stories.text: Justin Walley turns in the Colts' best game
stories.summary: Walley earned the top PFF grade on the team at 91.3. His strip-sack set up Adetomiwa Adebawore's fumble-return touchdown and a 21-7 lead. He played 54 snaps, starting in the slot and sliding outside once Ward left.

stories.text: 41.5: Daniel Jones' passer rating in a win
stories.summary: Jones went 11 of 22 for 108 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions, one of them returned 59 yards for a Miami score. NFL.com calls it the worst passer rating of his career in a win.

stories.text: Short week at Houston on Thursday
stories.summary: Indianapolis visits Houston on Thursday, Nov. 19 at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. Watch the cornerback and tackle injuries and whether Jones protects the ball.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars roll Titans and lead South by four

stories.text: Lawrence lifts Jaguars to 40-23 win in Nashville
stories.summary: Trevor Lawrence threw for 352 yards and three touchdowns as Jacksonville moved to 7-2. The Jaguars have scored 30 or more in four straight games and lead the AFC South by four games. They also set a franchise record with a fifth straight win against division opponents.

stories.text: Striggow in concussion protocol, Hainsey hurts knee
stories.summary: Danny Striggow was evaluated for a concussion and did not return. Robert Hainsey hurt his left knee and also left the game. Neither has a Week 11 status yet.

stories.text: Parker Washington posts a career-high 152 yards
stories.summary: Washington caught seven passes for 152 yards and a touchdown, and 148 of those yards came before halftime. Lawrence spread the ball to nine different receivers.

stories.text: 4: straight games with 30 or more points
stories.summary: Jacksonville matched its longest 30-point streak, set in 2017. Its 125-point differential is the best in the NFL, per NFL.com.

stories.text: Trip to face the Giants on Sunday
stories.summary: Jacksonville visits the New York Giants on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Watch the offensive line, with Hainsey's knee in question.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Titans fall to 1-8 and remain winless at home

stories.text: Titans lose 40-23 to Jacksonville at Nissan Stadium
stories.summary: Jacksonville pulled away in the second half, and Tennessee dropped to 1-8. The Titans have lost three straight and are winless at home in the final season at Nissan Stadium.

stories.text: Adams has a concussion, Robinson an ankle injury
stories.summary: Tony Adams suffered a concussion and Wan'Dale Robinson hurt an ankle against Jacksonville. Guard Peter Skoronski and punter Tommy Townsend are on injured reserve. Tennessee has not posted a Week 11 report.

stories.text: Cam Ward throws two touchdowns in a losing effort
stories.summary: Ward completed 28 of 39 passes for 231 yards, two touchdowns and an interception, and led the team with 39 rushing yards. He threw a 32-yard score to Tony Pollard and a 2-yard score to Daniel Bellinger.

stories.text: 35.7%: Titans play-action rate, a season high
stories.summary: Tennessee used play action on 35.7% of Ward's dropbacks, its highest rate this season, per NFL.com. The quarterback showed better accuracy and reads, though he threw an early interception.

stories.text: Sunday trip to Dallas
stories.summary: Tennessee visits the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX. Watch whether the play-action usage carries over on the road.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Broncos rest at 7-2 with five straight wins

stories.text: Broncos use the bye to protect a 7-2 start
stories.summary: Denver sits at 7-2 on a five-game winning streak and holds the AFC's second seed. Sean Payton's teams are 4-0 going into a bye and 3-0 coming out of one. The Athletic's playoff simulator gives Denver a 57 percent shot at the AFC West title.

stories.text: Receiver Pat Bryant nears a return from ankle injury
stories.summary: Bryant went down with an ankle injury in Week 4 against San Francisco and has served the four games required on injured reserve. He was eligible to return after the bye, and reports pointed to a possible Week 11 return against the Raiders. Denver has not posted a Week 11 injury report yet, so his status is unconfirmed.

stories.text: Bo Nix still hunting a consistent stretch
stories.summary: Through six games Nix averaged 5.6 yards per attempt, down from 6.4 last year, and his EPA per dropback turned negative. Denver's offense ranked last in yards per play at that point. Nix says the team feels good at 7-2 but has things to clean up.

stories.text: 3.7%: Denver's sack rate allowed, lowest in the NFL
stories.summary: The Broncos protect Nix better than any team in the league. The offense still ranks 25th in success rate, which explains why wins have come through defense and close finishes.

stories.text: Raiders visit Denver on Sunday afternoon
stories.summary: Denver hosts Las Vegas on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS at Empower Field at Mile High. The Broncos average 28 points over their last three wins but rank 26th in rushing yards per game. Watch whether they can run against a Raiders team starting rookie Fernando Mendoza.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Mahomes throws five TDs in rout of Falcons

stories.text: Chiefs rout Falcons 35-13 to tie Denver
stories.summary: Kansas City beat Atlanta in Atlanta on Sunday and moved into a first-place tie with Denver at 7-2. Patrick Mahomes threw five touchdown passes, including one to newly acquired receiver Josh Downs. Atlanta fell to 3-7.

stories.text: Wiley, Smith, Kelce and Delane all hurt in Atlanta
stories.summary: Andy Reid said tight end Jared Wiley fractured his ankle and guard Trey Smith entered concussion protocol. Cornerback Mansoor Delane has a shoulder fracture, though Reid said he will be fine. Reports differ on Travis Kelce: ESPN lists an aggravated right ankle, while another report cites a calf issue on top of the ankle.

stories.text: Rookie Emmett Johnson steps in for Kenneth Walker
stories.summary: Johnson made his first start with Walker out with a groin injury. He carried 22 times for 101 yards and caught six passes for 70 yards and two touchdowns.

stories.text: 348: Mahomes' passing yards on 22 of 35 throws
stories.summary: Mahomes pushed the ball downfield and finished with five touchdown passes. Kansas City has started 7-2 or better in four of the last five seasons.

stories.text: Cardinals visit Arrowhead on Sunday
stories.summary: Kansas City hosts Arizona (3-7) on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1:00 p.m. ET on CBS. Watch the injury report for Smith, Kelce and Walker, since the offensive line and backfield both took hits.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Mendoza's debut ends in a 21-13 loss

stories.text: Seahawks sack Mendoza six times in 21-13 win
stories.summary: The Raiders fell to 4-6 in rookie Fernando Mendoza's first start. Las Vegas led 10-7 at halftime, then managed little after the break against Seattle's defense. The Raiders traded Kirk Cousins to Minnesota before the deadline and handed the job to the No. 1 overall pick.

stories.text: Brock Bowers hurt his ankle on the opening series
stories.summary: Bowers left the Seattle game with an ankle injury and did not return. Coach Klint Kubiak called it significant but day-to-day. His status for Sunday at Denver is unclear. He already came back from a knee scope earlier this season.

stories.text: Mendoza starts fast, then runs into a wall
stories.summary: Mendoza opened with a 10-yard touchdown run and went 11 of 13 in the first half. He finished 17 of 29 for 143 yards with no interceptions, plus 22 rushing yards. The sacks and a dead second half mark the lesson of his debut.

stories.text: 171: Jaxon Smith-Njigba's yards, more than the Raiders' offense
stories.summary: Seattle's receiver outgained Las Vegas by himself. The Raiders finished with 163 total yards and punted seven straight times. Ashton Jeanty ran for 18 yards.

stories.text: Raiders travel to Denver for Sunday's 4:25 kickoff
stories.summary: Las Vegas visits the 7-2 Broncos on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS. Mendoza makes his first road start. The Raiders need protection fixed fast against a Denver defense that is playing well.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Chargers finally win, beat Ravens 23-20

stories.text: Chargers end 11-game skid with 23-20 win in Baltimore
stories.summary: Los Angeles won on Monday night for its first victory in 331 days, since Dec. 21, 2025. Tarheeb Still forced a fumble on Baltimore's last drive and Elijah Molden recovered it. The Chargers fell from a 13 to a 7 percent chance at the No. 1 pick, per ESPN Analytics.

stories.text: McConkey, Njoku and Pipkins carried questionable tags
stories.summary: Ladd McConkey was questionable for the Ravens game with an unspecified injury, and tight end David Njoku, linebacker Denzel Perryman and tackle Trey Pipkins needed activation from injured reserve to play. Whether they played is not confirmed in this report, and no post-game updates were found yet.

stories.text: Omarion Hampton runs for 105 in the win
stories.summary: Hampton led a season-high 160 rushing yards for Los Angeles. The Chargers held Derrick Henry to 16 yards on 15 carries and gave up no rushing yards after halftime. They committed no turnovers after 19 giveaways earlier this year.

stories.text: 331: days between Chargers wins
stories.summary: Los Angeles became only the second team to win a Monday night game after starting 0-8 or worse. The 2013 Buccaneers were the other.

stories.text: Jets visit SoFi Stadium on Sunday
stories.summary: The Chargers host New York on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 4:05 p.m. ET on FOX. They then host New England in Week 12. A second straight win would be a first for this team since last season.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Five Dak TDs not enough in 46-40 loss

stories.text: Cowboys fall 46-40 to 49ers at home
stories.summary: Dallas dropped to 4-6 on Monday night, Nov. 16, when San Francisco won a 46-40 shootout at AT&T Stadium. Dak Prescott threw five touchdown passes, but the defense could not get stops. The loss leaves the Giants as the only NFC East team at .500 or better.

stories.text: Pickens and Porter had hamstring and foot issues
stories.summary: Before the 49ers game, George Pickens (hamstring) and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. (foot) had both missed the Colts game, and Stephen Jones would only say the team would see how the week went. Running back Tyler Goodson has a knee injury Jones said will cost him time. Pickens played Monday, so watch Wednesday's report for Porter and the others.

stories.text: Pickens goes for 145 and three scores
stories.summary: George Pickens caught 11 of 18 targets for 145 yards and three touchdowns against San Francisco. He did it after missing the Colts game with a hamstring problem. Prescott finished 30 of 51 for 343 yards, five touchdowns and one interception.

stories.text: 46: points the Cowboys allowed to the 49ers
stories.summary: Dallas gave up 46 points at home and still scored 40 of its own. Five Prescott touchdown passes were not enough to cover for the defense. The Cowboys are 4-6 with the Giants holding the head-to-head tiebreaker.

stories.text: Titans visit Dallas on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Tennessee comes to AT&T Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 22, with a 1 p.m. ET kickoff on FOX. Watch whether the Cowboys fix the defense in six days and whether Porter returns to the secondary.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Giants lose 24-21 but still lead the East

stories.text: Giants lose to Washington 24-21 on Thursday night
stories.summary: New York fell 24-21 to the Commanders at MetLife Stadium on Nov. 12 and dropped to 5-3-1. Washington held on after Jayden Daniels threw two late interceptions. The Giants still lead the NFC East because Dallas lost to San Francisco on Monday night.

stories.text: Skattebo is back; Tracy and Edmunds are out
stories.summary: Cam Skattebo returned from the hamstring injury that cost him the previous week and carried a heavy load. Tyrone Tracy Jr. is on injured reserve and Tremaine Edmunds has a season-ending chest injury. Safety Pinnock went into the game questionable with a back problem.

stories.text: Skattebo piles up 122 yards and two touchdowns
stories.summary: Cam Skattebo finished with 122 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns in his return from the hamstring injury. His snap rate far exceeded his previous career high of 77 percent. Isaiah Likely added nine catches for 127 yards.

stories.text: 127: Isaiah Likely's career-high receiving yards
stories.summary: Likely caught nine passes for a career-best 127 yards against Washington. That total included a 66-yard touchdown that gave the Giants the lead in the fourth quarter. It was not enough, since Washington answered late.

stories.text: Jaguars visit MetLife on Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET
stories.summary: Jacksonville comes to MetLife Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 22. The league moved kickoff from 1 p.m. to 4:25 p.m. ET, and the game airs on CBS. The Giants need to bounce back to protect their division lead.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Eagles return from bye on a seven-game skid

stories.text: Eagles come off the bye at 2-7
stories.summary: Philadelphia returns from its Week 10 bye with seven straight losses. The Athletic gives the team less than a 1 percent chance at the playoffs. Jalen Hurts is out for the season and Lane Johnson retired earlier this year.

stories.text: Smith and Wicks expected back after bye
stories.summary: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) missed the three games before the bye and are both expected to return. Jihaad Campbell missed the last couple of games and Jonathan Greenard has struggled to recover from an ankle injury. Saquon Barkley has dealt with a stinger, a hamstring injury and a back injury.

stories.text: Barkley has 296 yards on 69 carries in seven games
stories.summary: Saquon Barkley averages 4.3 yards per carry with three touchdowns across seven games. Over the last two games he ran 26 times for 52 yards and two scores. He has been slowed by a stinger, a hamstring injury and a back injury.

stories.text: 582: Zach Ertz's receptions as an Eagle
stories.summary: Ertz sits seven catches behind Harold Carmichael's franchise record of 589. He currently sits on the practice squad, so the chase depends on a call up.

stories.text: Steelers visit Philadelphia Sunday at 1 p.m. ET
stories.summary: Pittsburgh plays at Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday, Nov. 22. The league moved kickoff from 4:25 p.m. to 1 p.m. ET and the game airs on CBS. Watch how the offense looks with Smith and Wicks back.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Commanders survive Daniels' picks to beat Giants

stories.text: Commanders edge Giants 24-21 on the road
stories.summary: Washington won at MetLife Stadium on Thursday, Nov. 12, and improved to 3-5-1. Jayden Daniels threw two interceptions late in the fourth quarter, then led a late touchdown that kept the team alive in the NFC East race. Washington is still two games behind the Giants.

stories.text: McLaurin out, Okonkwo returns after back scare
stories.summary: Terry McLaurin is out indefinitely with a knee injury. Tight end Chig Okonkwo hurt his back early in the second quarter and returned for the second half, while Colson Yankoff was ruled out with a knee injury. Daniels played through a left elbow injury after practicing fully all week.

stories.text: Daniels survives two late picks and finishes the job
stories.summary: Jayden Daniels threw two interceptions in the fourth quarter at MetLife Stadium. He still delivered a late touchdown that decided the game, 24-21. He played with a left elbow injury and practiced fully all week.

stories.text: 3-5-1: Washington's record after beating the Giants
stories.summary: The Commanders entered the Giants game at 2-5-1. The win moved them to 3-5-1 and kept them in the NFC East race, with Dallas also at 4-6.

stories.text: Bengals visit Washington Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN
stories.summary: Cincinnati comes to Washington for Monday Night Football on Nov. 23, with kickoff at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. Washington gets an extra day to heal before it plays.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Bears rest at 7-2 and slip to third

stories.text: Bears sit at 7-2 but lose the division lead on their bye
stories.summary: Chicago did not play in Week 10 and watched Detroit and Minnesota both win to pull level at 7-2. The Bears now sit third in the NFC North and sixth in the conference. They return Sunday at home against New Orleans, with the NFL's toughest remaining schedule ahead.

stories.text: Monangai still working back from a Week 5 injury
stories.summary: Running back Kyle Monangai has missed games since Week 5. He practiced on a limited basis in Week 9 and it remains unclear whether he plays against New Orleans. Receiver Zavion Thomas is likely to sit a game or two after a Week 9 penalty.

stories.text: Swift leads the league with 10 rushing touchdowns
stories.summary: D'Andre Swift carries the NFL's third-best rushing attack into the second half. Luther Burden III has 49 catches for 644 yards and four touchdowns, and he and Rome Odunze are both on pace for 1,000 yards.

stories.text: 10: points Chicago is favored by against the Saints
stories.summary: The Bears opened as 10-point favorites over New Orleans, their first line of eight points or more since 2020. The Saints are 3-6, but the Bears have allowed the most pass plays of 40 yards or more in the league.

stories.text: Saints visit Soldier Field on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET
stories.summary: Chicago hosts New Orleans on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 1 p.m. ET. A win sets up 8-2 before the Thanksgiving game against Detroit. Watch whether Monangai returns and whether the secondary stops giving up long throws. The TV network was not listed in the sources.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions rout Patriots, then lose Hutchinson

stories.text: Lions crush Patriots 35-10 in Munich for fifth straight win
stories.summary: Detroit rolled New England in Germany and moved into a tie for first in the NFC North at 7-2. The defense held the Patriots to 151 total yards, and Drake Maye left the game in the first quarter with an ankle injury.

stories.text: Hutchinson leaves with a knee injury, no diagnosis yet
stories.summary: Aidan Hutchinson hurt his right knee on the opening drive and did not return. No diagnosis had been announced after the game. Safety Kerby Joseph and cornerback D.J. Reed also missed the game.

stories.text: Gibbs piles up 252 total yards and two touchdowns
stories.summary: Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 153 yards and caught passes for 99 more in Munich, with 171 scrimmage yards in the first half alone. He now has 1,384 scrimmage yards and 13 touchdowns through nine games.

stories.text: 151: total yards the Lions allowed to New England
stories.summary: Detroit's defense held the Patriots to minus-1 yard on six straight drives to close the first half. Derrick Moore had two sacks, and Roger McCreary added an interception.

stories.text: Buccaneers visit Ford Field on Sunday at 1 p.m.
stories.summary: Detroit hosts Tampa Bay on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 1 p.m. on FOX. A short week follows, with Chicago coming to town for Thanksgiving. Watch how the pass rush holds up without Hutchinson.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Packers swept by Vikings, now on bye

stories.text: Vikings beat Packers 30-10 and sweep the season series
stories.summary: Minnesota outscored Green Bay 69-32 across the two games this year. The Packers fell to 6-4 and trail the division leaders in the loss column. CBS Sports graded the performance an F.

stories.text: Parsons still on PUP list as Rams game nears
stories.summary: Micah Parsons remains on the reserve/physically unable to perform list inside his 21-day practice window, and the Packers' Inbox column points to a Week 12 return. Before the Minnesota game, Josh Jacobs (finger) and Lukas Van Ness (back) missed practice, and Javon Bullard returned Friday in a limited role.

stories.text: Love takes eight sacks in a bruising day
stories.summary: Jordan Love went down eight times against Minnesota, tying the most for a Packers quarterback in 40 years. The run game gave him little help, and the Vikings forced four turnovers.

stories.text: 60%: share of Love's dropbacks that brought pressure
stories.summary: Pressure arrived on 60 percent of Love's dropbacks, a career high. Minnesota's defense also had its first game with eight sacks and four takeaways since 1989.

stories.text: Bye in Week 11, then Rams on Netflix Nov. 25
stories.summary: Green Bay is off Sunday, Nov. 22. The Packers play at the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday, Nov. 25, at 8 p.m. ET on Netflix at SoFi Stadium. Watch the offensive line and whether Parsons returns.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Vikings sack Love eight times at Lambeau

stories.text: Vikings beat Packers 30-10, pull level atop the NFC North
stories.summary: Minnesota ended a two-game skid and improved to 7-2, tied with Detroit and Chicago. Kirk Cousins threw two touchdown passes, both to backups, and the defense forced four takeaways at Lambeau Field.

stories.text: Hockenson, Jennings and Cashman sat out at Lambeau
stories.summary: T.J. Hockenson, Jauan Jennings, Jordan Addison and Blake Cashman were all out against Green Bay. A Star Tribune headline said Addison needs thumb surgery, but the article body did not confirm it.

stories.text: Jefferson hauls in nine catches on 12 targets
stories.summary: Justin Jefferson posted a season-high nine receptions for 74 yards against Green Bay. Myles Price added a 38-yard touchdown on third-and-23 and 70 kick return yards.

stories.text: 8: sacks of Jordan Love, a Vikings high at Lambeau
stories.summary: Seven different Vikings recorded a sack, with Levi Drake Rodriguez getting two. Five of the eight came in the first half, and Minnesota also took the ball away four times.

stories.text: 49ers in Mexico City on Sunday night, Nov. 22
stories.summary: Minnesota faces San Francisco at Estadio Banorte on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 8:20 p.m. ET. Fox Sports and the Fox 9 schedule list NBC; DAZN lists NFL Network, so the network is worth rechecking. Atlanta visits the following week.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Chiefs rout Falcons, who now take a bye

stories.text: Chiefs bury Falcons 35-13 as losing streak hits three
stories.summary: Patrick Mahomes threw five touchdown passes as Kansas City led 28-3 in the fourth quarter. Atlanta sits last in the NFC South at 3-7. Kevin Stefanski called the bye a chance to self-scout and learn some hard lessons.

stories.text: London clears concussion check, Deablo sits again
stories.summary: Receiver Drake London left the Chiefs game for a concussion evaluation and was cleared. Linebacker Divine Deablo, who has a fractured right forearm, was inactive against Kansas City. The bye should give his arm extra time to heal.

stories.text: Penix throws for 286 yards in a lost cause
stories.summary: Michael Penix Jr. completed 23 of 43 passes for 286 yards and one interception against Kansas City. He has thrown one touchdown pass in his last three games. Stefanski took responsibility for the offense and did not put the loss on his quarterback.

stories.text: 13: Interceptions thrown by Falcons quarterbacks, most in the NFL
stories.summary: Atlanta's turnover margin is minus 10, tied for second worst in the league. The Falcons also drew nine penalties for 65 yards against Kansas City, six of them on offensive linemen. Ball security and discipline top the list for the bye week.

stories.text: Bye in Week 11, then a trip to Minnesota
stories.summary: Atlanta is off this week. The next game is at the Minnesota Vikings on Nov. 29, followed by a game against the Lions. Watch whether the bye cleans up the turnovers and penalties.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Panthers win on a last-play kick, take the division lead

stories.text: Fitzgerald's 54-yarder lifts Panthers past Saints 20-17
stories.summary: Ryan Fitzgerald kicked a 54-yard field goal as time expired after a 30-yard pass interference call on Kool-Aid McKinstry. Carolina moved to 4-5 and took first place in the NFC South. The Panthers won despite 17 penalties.

stories.text: Brooks, Christensen and Jackson stay on injured reserve
stories.summary: Running back Jonathon Brooks, lineman Brady Christensen and defensive back Mike Jackson were not activated against New Orleans, even after practice windows opened. Carolina also hopes to get tackle Ickey Ekwonu back in the coming weeks. Cornerback Jaycee Horn likely will not play until December.

stories.text: Hubbard accounts for 172 yards and two scores
stories.summary: Chuba Hubbard ran 27 times for 92 yards and two touchdowns and caught five passes for 80 yards. Bryce Young added 17 of 30 for 200 yards with no turnovers. Hubbard carried the offense on a day the passing game stayed modest.

stories.text: 17: Penalties Carolina committed and still won
stories.summary: The Panthers drew 17 flags for 152 yards, compared with three for 46 yards for New Orleans. The defense held the Saints to 222 total yards and sacked Tyler Shough three times. Cleaning up the flags is the obvious fix.

stories.text: Ravens visit Charlotte Sunday at 1 p.m. on FOX
stories.summary: Carolina hosts Baltimore (4-5) on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX at Bank of America Stadium. The Panthers will try to protect their new hold on first place in the division.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints lose on the final kick, fall to 3-6

stories.text: Saints tie it late, then lose to Panthers on a last-play kick
stories.summary: Charlie Smyth's 55-yard field goal tied the game at 17 with 41 seconds left. A 30-yard pass interference call on Kool-Aid McKinstry then set up Carolina's winning 54-yarder. New Orleans dropped to 3-6, including 0-2 in the division and 1-4 at home.

stories.text: Werner and Richards both hurt in the loss
stories.summary: Starting linebacker Pete Werner left in the first half with a hamstring injury. Right tackle Asim Richards hurt his knee in the second half. Running back Travis Etienne Jr. returned from a hamstring injury and carried eight times for 14 yards.

stories.text: Rookie Jordyn Tyson catches 11 passes against Carolina
stories.summary: Tyson caught 11 passes for 80 yards, while Chris Olave had three receptions for 30 yards. Tyler Shough threw for 187 yards but was intercepted once and lost a fumble. Alvin Kamara scored both New Orleans touchdowns.

stories.text: 15.5: Sacks from Chase Young and Carl Granderson combined
stories.summary: Young has eight sacks and Granderson has 7.5 through the first half of the season, giving New Orleans one of the league's best edge pairs. Granderson added another sack against Carolina. Defensive coordinator Brandon Staley credited edge coach Jay Rodgers.

stories.text: Saints head to Chicago on Sunday at 1 p.m. on FOX
stories.summary: New Orleans plays at the Bears on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX. Watch the status of Werner and Richards, and whether the pass rush can keep producing on the road.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Bucs come off bye with Mayfield's ankle in question

stories.text: Bucs sit 3-6 but only a half game out of first
stories.summary: Tampa Bay lost 27-24 to Chicago on a walk-off field goal before its Week 10 bye. All six of its losses came by seven points or fewer. The NFC South race is still wide open, and the Bucs trail the leader by a half game.

stories.text: Mayfield's foot and ankle leave his status uncertain
stories.summary: Baker Mayfield hurt his foot and ankle against the Bears and spent parts of the bye week in a walking boot. Sources say the injury is not long-term and injured reserve is not under consideration. He has not been ruled out for Detroit.

stories.text: Bucky Irving carries the ground game
stories.summary: Irving has 825 rushing yards on 167 carries, a 4.9-yard average, with seven rushing touchdowns. Kenny Gainwell adds 305 yards at 4.8 per carry. Emeka Egbuka leads the receivers with 278 yards in seven games.

stories.text: 21: Takeaways by the Bucs defense, most in the NFL
stories.summary: Tampa Bay also leads the league with 16 interceptions. The defense forced 13 takeaways over Weeks 7 through 9, the most of any team in that stretch, including four interceptions against Chicago.

stories.text: Bucs visit Detroit Sunday at 1 p.m. on FOX
stories.summary: Tampa Bay plays at the Lions on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX at Ford Field. Mayfield's availability is the main question. A Week 12 home game against Carolina follows on Nov. 30.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Cardinals sink to 3-7 behind a rookie QB

stories.text: Rams bury Cardinals 34-6 in Carson Beck's first start
stories.summary: Arizona lost its 11th straight home game on Sunday, a 427-day streak that sits three short of the league record of 14. Beck, a third-round rookie who was the emergency third-string quarterback two weeks ago, started because Jacoby Brissett was traded to Baltimore on Nov. 6 and Gardner Minshew went down with a season-ending elbow injury. The offense managed 123 total yards.

stories.text: Wilson and Johnson Jr. done for the year
stories.summary: Receiver Michael Wilson and left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. both suffered season-ending injuries, according to Arizona Sports. Defensive lineman Jordan Burch left the Rams game in the first quarter with a knee injury and did not return. The outlet reports he is out for the season with an MCL injury.

stories.text: Carson Beck takes his first NFL snaps as a starter
stories.summary: The rookie from Miami finished 11 of 18 for 108 yards with two interceptions and no touchdowns. He arrived with a supporting cast already thinned by injuries and played behind a line that lost its left tackle for the season.

stories.text: 11: straight home losses for Arizona
stories.summary: The Cardinals have not won at home in 427 days. The league record is 14 straight. They also gained only 123 total yards against the Rams.

stories.text: At Kansas City, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Arizona travels to Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 22 for a regional CBS broadcast. Watch who lines up at quarterback and how many starters remain on the line and at receiver.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Rams roll to a fourth straight win, then rest

stories.text: Rams blow out Cardinals 34-6 for fourth straight win
stories.summary: Los Angeles improved to 6-4 on Sunday at State Farm Stadium without its top two receivers. The defense allowed no touchdown for the second week in a row. The Rams now head into a bye week, still tied with Green Bay and Seattle for the last NFC playoff spot.

stories.text: Nacua on IR, two centers hurt against Arizona
stories.summary: Puka Nacua is on injured reserve and Davante Adams was out as well. Centers Coleman Shelton (hamstring) and Dylan McMahon (knee) both left in the first half, which forced Beaux Limmer to play center and McVay to start the second half with six offensive linemen.

stories.text: Blake Corum runs for 100 yards and a score
stories.summary: Corum carried 17 times for 100 yards and a touchdown, his second 100-yard game of the season. He also caught three passes as the Rams leaned on two-back looks. Matthew Stafford added 249 yards and three touchdowns through the air.

stories.text: 9: Rams players caught a Stafford pass
stories.summary: With Nacua and Adams out, Stafford spread 18 completions across nine different receivers. He finished 18 of 26 for 249 yards, three touchdowns and one interception.

stories.text: Bye week for the Rams
stories.summary: Los Angeles is off in Week 11 after its fourth straight win. The recap does not name the opponent after the bye, so that game is not confirmed here. The Rams enter the break tied with Green Bay and Seattle for the final NFC playoff spot.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: 49ers go 8-1 and fly to Mexico City

stories.text: 49ers outlast Cowboys 46-40 in a shootout
stories.summary: San Francisco gained 584 yards, its most in a game in 14 years, and stayed on top of the NFC at 8-1. The game was Sunday, Nov. 15, not Monday. Kyle Shanahan still grumbled about five sacks allowed and two pre-snap penalties. The Vikings, owners of the NFL's top defense, are next.

stories.text: Green day to day; Evans, Hobbs, West nearing returns
stories.summary: Cornerback Renardo Green (back) left the Dallas game early and is day to day. Receiver Mike Evans (Achilles tendinitis) may practice this week after missing three games. Cornerback Nate Hobbs (adductor) and defensive tackle C.J. West (knee) are practicing and could come off injured reserve.

stories.text: Christian McCaffrey piles up 223 yards and 3 TDs
stories.summary: McCaffrey caught four passes for 161 yards, including touchdowns of 74 and 66 yards, and ran 13 times for 62 yards and a fourth-quarter score. The 74-yarder was the longest receiving touchdown of his career. He now holds the 49ers record with 21 receiving touchdowns by a running back or fullback.

stories.text: 389: Brock Purdy's passing yards in Dallas
stories.summary: Purdy went 22 of 28 for 389 yards and three touchdowns, per the Fox Sports box score. That box score lists the team's passing total as 370, so the two figures do not match. He also had 135 passing yards on scramble plays, including the 74-yard throw to McCaffrey.

stories.text: Vikings in Mexico City, Sunday at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC
stories.summary: San Francisco plays Minnesota on Sunday, Nov. 22 at Estadio Azteca, a 5:20 p.m. PT kickoff on NBC's Sunday Night Football. The 49ers will practice in Colorado Springs first. Watch their top-two offense against a Vikings defense that took Green Bay for eight sacks.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Seahawks beat Vegas, then take a bye

stories.text: Seahawks win 21-13 in Las Vegas, sack Mendoza six times
stories.summary: Seattle improved to 6-4 on Sunday at Allegiant Stadium and spoiled rookie Fernando Mendoza's first start. Drew Lock threw for 240 yards and two touchdowns in place of Sam Darnold. The Seahawks are tied with the Rams and Packers for the last NFC playoff spot going into their bye.

stories.text: Darnold expected back after the bye; Lucas, Holani hurt
stories.summary: Darnold has been dealing with quad and rib injuries, and the Seahawks believe he is on track to return for Week 12 after the bye. Against the Raiders, right tackle Abraham Lucas got hurt in the second quarter and running back George Holani (knee) left in the first. Left guard Quenton Nelson (knee) and left tackle Charles Cross (ankle) were inactive.

stories.text: Jaxon Smith-Njigba: 8 catches, 171 yards, 71-yard TD
stories.summary: Smith-Njigba had one catch for 11 yards at halftime, then exploded after the break, including a 71-yard touchdown in the third quarter. He ranks first in the league in receiving yards and touchdowns, according to KOMO.

stories.text: 6: sacks of Fernando Mendoza
stories.summary: Seattle sacked the Raiders rookie six times and held him to 143 passing yards. Las Vegas netted negative yardage on five of its six second-half drives.

stories.text: Bye in Week 11, then at San Francisco Nov. 29
stories.summary: Seattle is off this week. The Seahawks visit the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29. Coach Mike Macdonald is optimistic Darnold gets a full week of practice coming out of the break. Kickoff time and network are not confirmed in the sources read.
